sources.title: Vispark Lab public model roster
sources.evidence: Live unauthenticated GET identifies vispark/vision-large, owned_by vispark, 1000000 context, text/image/audio/video/file inputs, text output, tools, reasoning and structured outputs. Its created field is metadata, not an explicit availability statement. Reopened October 27: the exact Large record has no learned-model total or active-parameter field.

sources.title: Vispark Lab deployed API documentation
sources.evidence: The application bundle documents Vision sizes small, medium and large; PDF input, text output, one-million-token context, tool calls, and the exact vispark/vision-large identifier. Continual-learning weights are state returned by the hosted API. Fresh October 27 bundle review found no separate physical total or active parameter specification.

sources.title: Vision AI by Vispark: a foundational Indian multimodal AI
sources.evidence: September 1, 2025 article says the API is available in small, medium and large sizes. It establishes availability by this date, not the first release of the large variant.

sources.title: Vispark timeline and Terms of Service in deployed application
sources.evidence: Timeline distinguishes the August 2022 Vision Telegram bot, May 15, 2024 generic chat launch, and August 29, 2025 Lab launch. It does not date individual sizes. Terms reserve the service and its features to Vispark/licensors and restrict reproduction and distribution.

sources.title: A Culturally Aware Multimodal AI Model
sources.publisher: Vansh Kumar / Journal of Current Trends in Computer Science Research
sources.evidence: Reopened October 27. The July 2024 author paper repeatedly describes a 175B Vision model and decoder-only Transformer. It neither names CLv1 nor maps this earlier model to the current Large alias, and gives no separate active count.

sources.title: A Self-Improving Experiential AI Model: A Path to Continual Learning
sources.publisher: Vansh Kumar and M. Tanusri / Vispark Research Lab
sources.evidence: Reopened October 27. The November 2025 paper reports 250B Vision Experiential in its abstract and architecture introduction, but also labels the Vision base 175B in its introduction and specification list. Neither figure is an explicit CLv1 Large specification; no active-parameter count is given.

sources.title: Vision CLv1 model specifications and family
sources.evidence: Reopened October 27 by direct HTTP. The current developer page names founder Vansh Kumar and labels Vision CLv1 as a 550B foundational engine; its family table explicitly gives CLv1 550B, Medium 175B and Small 45B. It provides no separate activated count. The playground links to Vispark Lab; these are nominal developer specifications.

sources.title: Continual Learning Models: An Introduction to Weight Management
sources.evidence: Fresh October 27 search retrieved the complete indexed first-party article, crawled last month; direct HTTP and web-open attempts timed out. The abstract and section 3 call the base Vision CLv1 model 550B. Section 6 says the three models were trained from scratch, lists CLv1 550B, Medium 175B and Small 45B, and identifies all three as live at Vispark Lab. Its modified-Transformer and experience-state discussion supplies no active count. Section 4 links the exact Vision Large evaluation repository.

sources.title: Vision CLv1 ARC-AGI-3 evaluation repository
sources.evidence: Reopened October 27. The developer repository identifies its ARC-AGI-3 agent as driven by Vispark/Vision Large, defaults play-size to large, and connects to the Vispark Vision endpoint. README, API client and harness architecture describe returned continual-learning state but disclose no separate total or active count. This is the explicit CLv1-to-Large mapping, not a parameter-size inference from older Vision papers.

sources.title: Original Vision Large catalog record
sources.evidence: Upstream comments explicitly derive May 15, 2024 from the model-roster created timestamp. This explains the unsupported release-date interpretation; it is not primary availability evidence.

sources.title: Vision CLv1 evaluation API client
sources.evidence: Fresh October 27 source sets the Vispark /model/text/vision endpoint, accepts small/medium/large sizes and returns a weights string; no parameter-count or activation convention is defined.

sources.title: Vision CLv1 evaluation harness architecture
sources.evidence: Fresh October 27 source describes an agent control loop and continual-learning state lifecycle, not learned-model tensor dimensions or activated-parameter counts. The exploration and competition phases do not establish different model parameter counts.

sources.title: AIVOCO model library
sources.evidence: Fresh October 27 developer catalog identifies Vision CLV1 and inference-time weight updates separately from an older Vision listing. It gives no numerical total or active count and no unchanged-base lineage from the older model.

sources.title: AIVOCO published research index
sources.evidence: Fresh October 27 research index links the Experiential Learning and Vision multimodal papers. It contains no active count or later parameter-comparison table; the linked historical papers are not named CLv1 Large specifications.

sources.title: Vision public launch announcement: Small, Medium and Large API availability
sources.evidence: Fresh full original article dated September 1, 2025 is presented as the Vision introduction and explicitly offers immediate API access through Vispark Lab in small, medium and large sizes. It therefore documents the public launch of all three named sizes, not only generic future plans. The separate August 29 Lab platform milestone does not name the sizes, and later CLv1 specifications are not evidence of their 2025 checkpoint sizes.

sources.title: Vispark official timeline: Lab platform launch
sources.evidence: Fresh deployed timeline content identifies August 29, 2025 as Lab launch with 14 models across modalities, without enumerating the Vision sizes. It separately identifies May 15, 2024 as generic Vision chat launch and May 15, 2025 as its relaunch. None overrides the September 1 introduction that explicitly offers the three API sizes.

name.note: The exact roster identifier is vispark/vision-large; remove the provider prefix from its display name.

developer.note: The API identifies Vispark as owner. Later CLv1 material is published by AIVOCO and founder Vansh Kumar and points back to Vispark Lab.

family.note: The documented Vision API has small, medium and large sizes.

release_date.note: The developer’s dated September 1 introduction explicitly launches Vision and offers immediate native API access in small, medium and large sizes, including Large. Use this documented public launch; the August 29 Lab platform launch does not identify these sizes and the May 2024 created timestamp is generic chat metadata. This dates the API alias, not the later CLv1 checkpoint or its undated backend transition.

open_weights.note: The documented distribution is a hosted proprietary base model. Returned continual-learning state and the MIT evaluation harness are not downloadable base-model weights.

license.note: Descriptive classification for the hosted base model: the developer calls its core proprietary and reserves service rights. The evaluation harness license does not license model weights.

parameters_b.note: Fresh October 27 review retains the developer-published nominal 550B for current Vision CLv1 Large: the family table and article give the size, and the article-linked evaluation explicitly uses Vispark/Vision Large. The article says CLv1 was trained from scratch; no unchanged-base count is transferred from the older 175B/250B Vision papers.

active_parameters_b.note: Fresh separate review of the current family specifications, complete indexed CLv1 article, exact API/client, research index, historical papers and later comparison searches found no explicit active-parameter count for CLv1 Large. Updating or returning experience weights does not specify per-token participation; the nominal 550B total is not substituted for an active count.

architecture.note: The linked CLv1 technical article explicitly describes a modified Transformer. Dense versus mixture-of-experts structure is not established; no such subtype is inferred from the total count.

context_window.note: The exact live roster reports context_length 1000000, consistent with the shared size-specific API documentation.

modalities.note: The exact roster lists text/image/audio/video/file input and text output; Lab documentation identifies PDF among accepted files.

reasoning.note: The exact roster explicitly lists reasoning in supported_features. This verifies the provider declaration, not an independently benchmarked capability or always-on reasoning mode.

tool_call.note: The exact roster lists tools and the shared Vision request schema accepts function definitions for all three sizes.

patch.notes: Vision Large has a nominal developer-published 550B total for the later CLv1 model, linked through the developer’s evaluation repository. Active parameters and dense/MoE structure are not separately disclosed. Earlier Vision papers describe different generations and do not supply this count. The developer’s September 1, 2025 launch article explicitly offers the Large API; this dates the alias’s documented public launch, not its later CLv1 backend. The August 29 Lab launch does not enumerate these sizes, and generic May 2024 creation metadata is not used. Returned learning state and the open evaluation harness do not make the base weights open. Capabilities reflect provider documentation.

summary: Preserves current Vision Large API properties, Vision family, proprietary classification and Transformer assessment. Fresh October 27 parameter review confirms the developer’s nominal 550B CLv1 total through the current family table, technical article and exact Vision Large evaluation mapping; active parameters remain undisclosed after separate original-source and later-comparison searches. Fresh release-date review accepts September 1, 2025 as the documented public launch of the explicitly offered Large API. The later CLv1 transition remains undated; all thirteen other field assessments are preserved.

parameter_reaudit.outcome: Retain nominal parameters_b=550 verified from current developer CLv1 specifications; explicitly retain active_parameters_b=null undisclosed after fresh separate review.

fresh_originals.finding: Exact Large API entry has no total or active learned-model count.
Three native sizes and exact OpenAI-compatible model IDs; no physical parameter counts.
Earlier release article documents three sizes without assigning learned-model counts.
Repeated 175B historical Vision total, without CLv1 Large identity or active count.
Abstract and architecture introduction say 250B; base specification says 175B. Historical ambiguity is not transferred to current CLv1.
Current developer model specifications and family table identify nominal 550B CLv1; no active count.
Fresh complete indexed original article: abstract and section 3 give base 550B; section 6 explicitly maps three from-scratch models to live Vispark Lab access. No separate active count.
Article-linked original harness identifies Vispark/Vision Large and defaults play-size to large.
Client passes size to the Vispark Vision endpoint and handles returned state without parameter accounting.
Harness control and learning-state lifecycle provide no activation-size convention.
CLv1 and earlier Vision listings are distinct; no inherited-count relationship or active count.
Research index adds no later numerical active-count comparison.

parameter_reaudit.search_findings: Fresh bounded searches for total and active counts, named lineage and later original comparison tables found the current first-party family specifications and article, plus exact-model ARC evaluation evidence. No qualifying original comparison with an activated-parameter column was found. Secondary catalog results supplied no additional size evidence. The model library and article distinguish CLv1 from older Vision generations; the accepted 550B is a direct nominal specification, not an inference from those predecessors.
parameter_reaudit.access_limitations: The AIVOCO weight-management article timed out on a bounded direct HTTP retry and web open. Its complete indexed first-party text was freshly retrieved, with crawl recency shown as last month, and saved locally; the 550B nominal claim is also directly available on the current developer homepage. Other listed originals were fetched successfully on October 27. Fetch manifests: /tmp/parameter-late-model-originals/manifest.json and /tmp/parameter-519-fresh/manifest.json.
parameter_reaudit.remaining_uncertainty: A separate active count and dense/MoE subtype are not disclosed. The continual-learning state file has no published parameter-accounting convention; its serialized size is not added to the nominal base-model count. Earlier 175B/250B paper figures do not specify the current alias.

accessed_originals.method: direct HTML and linked deployed app bundle

findings: The September 1 publisher introduction contains launch language and immediate native availability for each of the three exact size names.
A separate August 29 platform launch says 14 models, but does not identify these sizes.
Current CLv1 specifications describe a later backend and are not backdated to this API-alias launch.
release_date_reaudit.outcome: Verified 2025-09-01, day precision, as the documented public API-size launch.
limitations: No immutable dated checkpoint or alias transition to later CLv1 is published in the reviewed sources. The public introduction establishes launch; undocumented earlier availability is not inferred.
